questions.question: What is the core operating invariant for a healthcare AI system?
options: Use it only inside its validated boundary and preserve a safe fallback
Keep the model online whenever latency is healthy
Replace human review when confidence exceeds 0.5
Retrain automatically after every drift alert
questions.explanation: Availability and confidence do not prove that the input, population, workflow, or use remains inside the evidence boundary.

questions.question: Why can positive predictive value change when sensitivity and specificity stay fixed?
options: It depends on outcome prevalence in the evaluated population
It depends only on model file size
It is always equal to sensitivity
It changes only when latency changes
questions.explanation: The share of positive results that are true positives depends on both the operating point and the prevalence of positives.

questions.question: Which split rule most directly reduces patient leakage in healthcare datasets?
options: Keep every record from one patient in only one split
Shuffle individual images across all splits
Split after feature normalization
Use the largest possible test set
questions.explanation: Correlated records from the same patient can make evaluation unrealistically easy when they appear in development and test data.

questions.question: A hospital changes an EHR unit mapping but leaves model weights untouched. What should the team conclude?
options: The system may still have changed because feature semantics and lineage changed
No validation is needed because the weights are identical
Only network latency can be affected
The model should silently learn the new unit
questions.explanation: A data-contract change can move the system outside its validated behavior even when the model artifact is unchanged.

questions.question: Which monitoring view best exposes hidden operational harm?
options: Outcomes, errors, overrides, abstentions, and workload by relevant slice
Average API latency alone
Training loss alone
Total prediction count without population context
questions.explanation: Technical health must be connected to workflow, outcome, and slice-level evidence to detect consequential failures.

questions.question: What does the change-control lab's result represent?
options: An educational engineering release posture, not legal or regulatory approval
FDA clearance
A clinical treatment recommendation
Proof that every patient population is covered
questions.explanation: The lab teaches evidence and containment decisions; real regulatory and clinical determinations require qualified professionals and applicable processes.
